terms.definition: A noun, pronoun, adjective, or verbal noun (maṣdar) that carries independent lexical meaning without being bound to tense.
A verb denoting an action or state tied to a grammatical tense/aspect (past māḍī, imperfect muḍāriʿ, or imperative amr).
A particle (preposition, conjunction, mood governor, or interrogative) whose meaning is realized in relation to nouns or verbs.
The unmarked grammatical state (marfūʿ), typically marked by ḍammah (-u/-un) on nouns and on indicative imperfect verbs.
The governed state (manṣūb), typically marked by fatḥah (-a/-an) on verbal objects/adverbials and on subjunctive imperfect verbs.
The noun-only case (majrūr) governed by prepositions (ḥurūf al-jarr) or annexation (iḍāfah), typically marked by kasrah (-i/-in).
The verb-only apocopated mood (majzūm) governed by lam, prohibitive lā, or conditional particles, marked by sukūn or deletion.
The nominative topic/subject that opens an equational nominal sentence (al-jumlah al-ismiyyah).
The predicate that completes a nominal sentence by giving information about the mubtadaʾ.
The nominative doer/agent of an active verb in a verbal sentence (al-jumlah al-fiʿliyyah).
The accusative noun or pronoun upon which the action of a transitive verb falls.
An annexation phrase linking a possessed noun (muḍāf, stripped of al- and tanwīn) to a genitive possessor (muḍāf ilayh).
A noun or adjective barred from tanwīn that takes ḍammah in the nominative and fatḥah in both accusative and genitive when indefinite.
A doubled short vowel (-un, -an, -in) at the end of a fully declinable indefinite noun.
The science of internal word structure, root derivation, and morphological patterns (awzān).
The science of clause structure, sentence boundaries, word order, and syntactic governance.
The vocalization of final case (on nouns) and mood (on verbs) vowels or letters reflecting syntactic governance.
A syntactic regent (such as a verb, preposition, inna, or conditional particle) that causes a word to take a specific case or mood.
A descriptive follower that agrees with its antecedent noun in four respects: gender, number, case, and definiteness.
An accusative noun, participle, or clause describing the state or manner of the subject or object during an action.
An indefinite accusative noun that clarifies ambiguity in quantity, dimension, counted numbers, or vague comparative statements.
A syntactic substitute or appositive that follows an antecedent (mubdal minhu) and shares its grammatical case without an intervening conjunction.
A clause attached to a relative pronoun (al-mawṣūl) containing a returning pronoun (al-ʿāʾid) that refers back to the antecedent.
A phonetic template based on the triliteral template f-ʿ-l (ف-ع-ل) representing metric weight, vocalic patterns, and augments.
